FOREWORD
Indian by the by the

Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Institution on 4 May 1979, after the draft finalized Standards Sectional Committee had been approved Division Council.

0.2 In testing laboratories, much avoidable duplication is encountered in nreparing and maintaining more than one solution of the same indicator when testing according to Indian :3r the same type of titration Standards. The Sectional Committee responsible for the preparation of this standard felt that it would be desirable to have a standard prescribThis standard is ing the preparation of the common indicator solutions. intended to serve as a ready guide for the preparation of indicator solutions. 0.3 This standard was first published in 196'2. This revision incorporates additional indicators which are now used in chemical analysis. 0.4 In the preparation of'this BS 4123 : 1967 Schedule of Standards-Institution. revision, assistance has been derived from British preferred chemical indicators.

Place 8'8 g of chemically pure o-aminophenol in a 3 OOO-ml comcal flask containing 2 000 ml of water at 80�C. After dissolution, add 8 g of a 300 g per litrc water solution of glyoxal. Keep the mixture at 80�C for 30 minutes, then Filter the precipitate so obtained cool to room temperature under running water. through a Buchner funnel and wash three times. carefully drying after each wash. Transfer the precipitate to a 250-ml beaker. Add 10 ml of acetone. After dissolution, add approximately 3 g of activated carbon, stir for one minute, then filter on a dry Auted filter paper and collect the filtrate in a 750-ml conical flask. Add.300 ml of water to the filtrate and filter the precipitate through a Buchncr Crusb Dry the residue thoroughly, in an oven at 70%. funnel employing suction. and store in a dark air-tight container.
